summary.headline: Medplus Q2 FY27 consolidated operating EBITDA was Rs 981 million (4.8%) on revenue of Rs 20,371 million, including a one-time Rs 79.6 million benefit.
summary.overview: Medplus added 166 net stores in Q2 FY27 (5,642 total, including 849 franchisee outlets), ahead of 146 in Q1. Consolidated operating EBITDA was Rs 981 million at 4.8%, or 4.4% excluding a Rs 79.6 million reversal of store retention bonus provision. Pharmacy revenue grew 21.3% YoY, and diagnostics revenue rose to Rs 410.5 million with a 23.8% EBITDA margin. Management guided FY27 operating EBITDA to roughly Rs 380-400 crore, below the earlier AOP, citing wage increases in several states.

segments.name: Pharmacy (retail stores)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 21.3% YoY with operating EBITDA of Rs 885 million (4.4%). Stores older than 12 months generated 93% of pharmacy revenue.

segments.name: Diagnostics
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 410.5 million, up about 23% YoY, with EBITDA of Rs 97.9 million at 23.8%. Subscriptions were about 216,000 active against a stated 300,000-400,000 threshold for further investment.

segments.name: Franchisee network
segments.commentary: Franchisee net revenue was Rs 116 crore in Q2 versus Rs 83 crore in Q1. Store count was 849 active, and 82 franchisee outlets were added net in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: FY27 operating EBITDA guided at roughly Rs 380-400 crore, versus the earlier AOP, due to wage increases in Karnataka, Telangana and other states (about Rs 7 crore per month, or Rs 80-85 crore for the year).
EBITDA margin expected around 4.8%, possibly up to 5% at most, in H2 FY27; management said it expects margin to improve sequentially.
Targeting 800 net new stores including franchisees in FY27; FY28 additions expected to be higher than 800.
Private label mix expected to rise by about 0.5 percentage points per quarter, combining pharma (0.2-0.3 pts) and non-pharma (0.1-0.2 pts).
Working capital expected to normalise to prior levels by year end.

Capex plans withdrawn; the focus is on store openings funded internally. Management said cost reduction of at least 0.5-0.75% is achievable over about four quarters through warehouse consolidation and AI-led automation.
capex_capacity: Store network at 5,642 stores (849 franchisee) spanning over 3 million sq ft; average store size about 539 sq ft.
Net store additions in Q2: 219 openings and 53 closures (14 relocations, 23 franchisee closures), for a net 166.
Around 29% of stores are under 2 years old and 71% are 2 years or older.
About 80 large-format stores are functional, with 70-80 more planned in FY27.
103 company stores converted to the franchisee model in Q2.
Warehouse consolidation planned to reduce duplicate warehouses in early-entry cities.
demand_pricing: Average daily prescription plans: 648 in July, 640 in August, 657 in September; around 2.16 lakh active plans as of 30 September.
Monthly sales run-rate is about Rs 650-670 crore, of which about 21% is private label; general goods about Rs 70 crore per month.

Discounts reduced slightly; management said the wage increase absorbed most of the benefit, and no other chain is following. Management described the discount reduction as a plan to raise discounts over time.

Private label non-pharma sales grew 18% QoQ after supply and pricing issues were fixed. Private label farmer (pharma) sales were flat to slightly down, with management saying staff had been pushing private label too hard and upsetting regular customers.
Management cited a store-level SSSG threshold of about 4% to keep a mature store steady, given rent up about 5% and store salaries up 6-7% a year.

qa_highlights.question: Are franchisees carrying a higher share of private label than company-owned stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said franchisee private label is expected to be lower initially, given newer stores, and it will split out franchisee numbers from next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will private label mix improvement continue at the previous pace?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 0.5 percentage points per quarter in combined private label mix, with non-pharma doing most of the lifting. Non-pharma was 10.7% of revenue, up from 9.8%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 EBITDA outlook after the wage increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided Rs 380-400 crore for FY27, or about 4.8-5% margin. Wage revisions in several states had pushed the AOP down.

qa_highlights.question: Is the franchisee model economics dilutive to margins?
qa_highlights.answer: On a Rs 100 MRP basis, Medplus retains about 10-11% gross margin on franchisee sales versus about 13-14% on company stores. Management said store-level margin is similar and that franchisee stores are mostly under 12 months old, so revenue per store is lower.

qa_highlights.question: What is the financial impact of the wage increases and what are the cost-saving levers?
qa_highlights.answer: The wage increase costs about Rs 7 crore per month, or Rs 80-85 crore a year. Cost levers are warehouse consolidation, AI-based back-end automation and product mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the diagnostics expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Further investment depends on reaching 300,000-400,000 annual subscriptions; the current base is about 216,000.

risks_watch: Wage inflation in Karnataka, Telangana and other states is pressuring store margins and cutting the FY27 EBITDA outlook.
Franchisee closures (23 in Q2) and lower revenue per franchisee store could weigh on store economics.
Working capital is rising, with first-year store inventory at 86 days and Q2 NWC at 54 days; management expects normalisation by year end.
Store age profile is weakening (71% of stores are 2+ years old, down from about 79%), which may dilute margins as expansion continues.
Promoter share pledging remains an overhang on the stock. Management said pledging depends on the share price and no immediate reduction is planned.
summary.management_tone: Confident on store expansion, private label growth and the 800-store target, but cautious on near-term margins, which management has cut from the AOP because of wage costs. Management was evasive on the pledge question and on the detailed EBITDA split by category, deferring both to follow-up.

The big difference was, yeah, the big difference was that the brand sale went up.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Targeting 800 net new stores in FY27 with 166 added in Q2 (219 openings, 53 closures) and 70-80 more large-format stores planned in FY27; FY28 additions guided above 800.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Pharmacy revenue up 21.3% YoY, mature-store SSSG guided at 9-10%, and prescription plans steady at about 640-657 per day, with 2.16 lakh active plans.

rows.label: New capex announcement

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 operating EBITDA was cut to Rs 380-400 crore from the earlier AOP because of Rs 80-85 crore of annual wage costs; only mature-store SSSG and store target were held.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 EBITDA already cut to Rs 380-400 crore on wage inflation; working capital at 54 days and first-year store inventory at 86 days could weigh further, though management expects normalisation by year end.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Private label mix is guided to rise about 0.5 percentage points per quarter (non-pharma 10.7% of revenue, up from 9.8%); no new product or brand launch was named.

rows.label: Warehouse consolidation and AI-led automation
rows.why: Management says at least 0.5-0.75% cost reduction is achievable over about four quarters, offsetting the Rs 80-85 crore wage cost.

rows.label: Diagnostics investment gated on subscriptions
rows.why: Diagnostics EBITDA margin is 23.8% on Rs 410.5m revenue, but further investment depends on reaching 300,000-400,000 subscriptions versus about 216,000 now.

rows.label: Working capital normalisation by year end
rows.why: NWC at 54 days with first-year store inventory at 86 days; management expects normalisation to prior levels by year end.

tone.note: Management was confident on store expansion, the 800-store target and private label growth, but cautious on margins after cutting FY27 EBITDA guidance for wage costs; analysts pressed on margins and the franchisee economics, and management was evasive on the pledge question.

oneOffs.what: Rs 79.6 million one-time reversal of store retention bonus provision in Q2 FY27 consolidated operating EBITDA

quality.why: Pharmacy revenue grew 21.3% YoY and store count rose by 166 net, with the brief not splitting volume from price, so growth looks largely volume-driven; the Rs 79.6 million one-time reversal flatters EBITDA (4.8% reported vs 4.4% excluding it), though it is a profit item rather than a revenue one.
